author: Tom
text:
# Hotel Code Mapping — Business & Feature Documentation

_Based on a full read of the oh-admin frontend module (`src/app/routes/ho-code-mapping/`) and the oh-api backend (`AdminHotelCodeMappingService`, `AdminRouter`). Written for non-technical readers first, with a technical mapping table at the end._

---

## Part 1 — What this screen is for (plain language)

Ohmyhotel buys hotel rooms from many suppliers — Agoda, EAN, Hotelbeds, DOTW, FITRuums, and others. **The same real-world hotel comes from several suppliers, each using its own code and its own spelling of the name.** For example, the "Victoria Hoi An Beach Resort" might arrive as code `146418` from FITRuums and a different code from Agoda.

If we did nothing, customers would see the _same hotel five times_. **Hotel Code Mapping is the back-office screen where staff link all those supplier versions to ONE internal hotel record**, so the customer sees a single clean hotel.

Three simple ideas:

* **Internal hotel** — our own single record for a real hotel (identified by a "Hotel Code").
* **Supplier hotel** — one supplier's version of that hotel (identified by supplier + supplier's hotel code).
* **Mapping** — the link that says _"this supplier hotel is really our internal hotel."_

A supplier hotel with no link yet is **"unmapped"** and needs a staff member to map it.

**Who uses it:** operations / content staff who curate hotel inventory.

**Why it matters:** correct mapping = no duplicate hotels for customers, and prices from all suppliers roll up under one hotel.

---

## Part 2 — What staff can do on the screen (features)

### 1. Search / filter supplier hotels

Find supplier hotels to work on. Filters: **Country** (required), Vendor, Hotel Name, Hotel Code, V.Hotel Code, Mapping status (mapped / unmapped), Address, Phone, Fax, Latitude, Longitude, V.City Name.

Results appear in a table showing both the supplier's data and, if already linked, our internal Hotel Code.

_(This is the search that was freezing the server — see ELS-2311. Sorting by column is turned off and the list always comes back newest-first.)_

### 2. Create a new master hotel — button **"New"**

Take one or more **unmapped** supplier hotels and create a **brand-new internal hotel** for them. Used when the hotel doesn't exist in our system yet.

* The system picks the "best" supplier to copy name/address from, in priority order: **Agoda → Hotelbeds → DOTW → FITRuums → others.**
* Blocked if any selected row is already mapped ("There is already a mapped hotel").

### 3. Add supplier hotels to an existing master hotel — button **"Add"**

Attach supplier hotels to an internal hotel that **already exists**. Used to add another supplier's version to a hotel we already have.

* The selection must contain **exactly one** already-mapped hotel (that supplies the target Hotel Code).

### 4. Delete a mapping — button **"Delete"**

Unlink selected supplier hotels from their internal hotel.

* All selected rows must share the same Hotel Code, and staff must confirm.
* **Safety rule:** the system refuses to delete if it would leave the internal hotel with **1 or fewer** suppliers — so a hotel is never left with no supplier ("orphan" protection).

### 5. View hotel detail — button **"Info"**

Open a popup with the mapped internal hotel's content/details. Only works for hotels that are already mapped.

### 6. Select rows & manage the selection

Tick rows with checkboxes; selected items show as removable chips, separating the mapped "root" hotel from candidate supplier hotels. A rule prevents mixing more than one already-mapped hotel in a selection.

### 7. Pagination

Page through results; page sizes 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 (default 20). Changing filters or page size returns to page 1.

_(Supporting data loaded automatically: the Vendor dropdown and the Star-Rating list.)_

_(A legacy "Region management" popup exists in the code but is currently disabled/unwired.)_

---

## Part 3 — Feature → Frontend → Backend map (technical)

| # | Feature | FE component / handler | NgRx action → effect | Backend endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Search | `search/…search.component` `onSubmit()` → container `clickSearchHandler` | `changeSearchConditionWithLimit` → (combineLatest) → `loadList` → `loadList$` | **POST** `/admin/hotel/code-mapping` → `getCodeMapping` |
| 2 | Create new hotel ("New") | `control/…control.component` `onClickCreate()` → `clickCreateHandler` | `createHotel` → `createHotel$` | **PUT** `/admin/hotel/code-mapping/add` → `addCodeMapping` |
| 3 | Add to existing ("Add") | control `onClickAdd()` → `clickAddHandler` | `addHotel` → `addHotel$` | **PUT** `/admin/hotel/code-mapping/save` → `saveCodeMapping` |
| 4 | Delete mapping ("Delete") | control `onClickDel()` → `clickDelHandler` | `removeHotel` → `removeHotel$` | **DELETE** `/admin/hotel/code-mapping/delete` → `deleteCodeMapping` |
| 5 | View detail ("Info") | control `onClickInfo()` → `clickInfoHandler` | `openInfoPopup` (state only) → `<app-hotel-detail>` | (hotel-detail module fetches its own data) |
| 6 | Row select / chips | `list-grid` `onCheckRow`, `selected` chips | `changeCheckedGridRow` / `clearCheckedGridRow` | none (client state) |
| 7 | Pagination | grid `onPageChange`, control `onChangePageSize` | `changeMainListPageAction` → `loadList` | same as #1 |
| — | Vendor dropdown | container `ngAfterContentInit` | `loadVendorsAction` → `loadVendors$` | **POST** `/common/comp` |
| — | Star-rating list | container `ngAfterContentInit` | `loadStarRatingList` → `loadStarRatingList$` | **POST** `/common/detail-code` |

### Backend business logic per write operation

* **add** (`/add`): if no internal Hotel Code exists yet → insert a new `HO_HOTEL_MASTER` (new internal hotel), then insert the mapping (`VD_VENDOR_HOTEL_MAPPING`); if the supplier is Agoda, refresh its average rating; push a change trigger and update 2 Redis lookup keys. Vendors processed in the priority order above.
* **save** (`/save`): same as add but the internal Hotel Code already exists (re-map / attach another supplier). Same priority + Redis + trigger logic.
* **delete** (`/delete`): refuses if the hotel would be left with ≤1 mapping ("error.hotel-code-mapping.delete"); removes the mapping and clears the 2 Redis keys.
* Note: Rakuten (910023) codes have a `_CSDUP_N` suffix stripped when building the Redis search key.

### Search request/response shape

* Request sends `condition.limits = [start, end]` (offset pagination) and **does not send a sort order** (server fixed order: `LAST_UPDATE_DATETIME desc, VENDOR_HOTEL_CODE asc`).
* Response returns `{ list, totalCount }`; the grid shows `totalCount` as the total.
* Search filters map to backend columns on `VD_VENDOR_HOTEL_MASTER` (+ mapping status via `VD_VENDOR_HOTEL_MAPPING`). Hotel Name / Address are text searches.

### ELS-2306 frontend changes already present in this branch

* Search button is disabled while a request is in flight; `onSubmit()` early-returns if `loading` is true (blocks duplicate Enter/double-click submissions that overwhelmed the server).
* Grid column sorting disabled (`[sortable]="false"`) and `sortOrder` removed from the request, so queries always hit the index and avoid the filesort/timeout.

### Minor code-hygiene notes (optional follow-up)

* `effects/ho-code-mapping.effects.ts` imports an unused `{ rejects } from 'assert'`.
* Leftover `console.log` in `createHotel$` and in the container's `checkedRowIds$` subscription.
* A few alert messages are still in Korean (`clickInfoHandler`, `onClickInfo`) while the rest are English.
* Because each successful write triggers `reloadListAction` → `onSubmit()`, and `onSubmit()` now early-returns while `loading`, a reload firing during an in-flight load could be silently skipped — worth a quick edge-case check.

# ELS-2037 — Staging A/B results for `getAdminVendorRateAllotmentV2` (hotel 251940)

## Executive summary (EN)

**What was tested.** A/B on staging (`test-admapi.ohmyhotel.com`), same deploy serving both versions on the same JVM/DB/Redis/data: `POST /admin/vendor/rate-allotment` (**optimized** V2) vs `.../legacy` (**pre-optimization**, verbatim from master). Hotel 251940, `yearMonth=202607`, default `allTrue` flags, ~5.6 MB response. Endpoint is the target of the "high CPU/memory" ticket; the core change is **8 DB connections/request → 1**.

**Verdict: MERGE.** The optimization is confirmed by three consistent, mechanistically-linked signals plus byte-identical output.

| Signal | Legacy | Optimized | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Correctness** (4 flag combos, normalized) | — | **identical** | Behavior-preserving; even `onSalesOnly` matches on staging |
| **HikariCP pending** (C=25) | **24** (pool 10/10 exhausted) | **3** | ~8× less — mirrors the 8→1 conn/req change |
| **Failure rate** under load (C=10 / C=20) | 11.8% / 28.9% | **0% / 20.5%** | Legacy's queued threads time out → non-2xx |
| **CPU avg** under load (C=25 / C=5) | 0.075 / 0.085 | **0.042 / 0.045** | ~44–47% lower; legacy pins a full core (peak 1.00) |

**What NOT to read from staging.** (1) Under-load **latency/throughput** is bandwidth-confounded — 5.6 MB payloads pulled from a remote client saturate the client's downlink at C≥10, not the server. (2) **Absolute CPU/heap** are noisy because staging runs ≥2 JVMs behind a load balancer (each metrics scrape hits a random instance) — read the _contrast_, not absolute values. Heap on staging differs only ~5% (within noise). The clean absolute CPU/heap numbers (**−22–36% CPU/RPS, −15–40% heap peak**) come from the earlier single-instance local run (`REPORT-FILLED.md`); staging confirms their _direction_.

**Trade-off (by design).** A single un-loaded request is _slower_ optimized (8.56s vs 5.35s) — sequential reads instead of 8-way parallel `Mono.zip`. The benefit appears only under concurrency (pool no longer exhausts).

**Reproduce.** `Run-Correctness.ps1` → `Run-Sweep.ps1` → `Run-Hikari.ps1 -Concurrency 25 -DurationSec 35` (all dot-source `config.ps1`; staging token there expires ~5h — swap on 401).

---

* **Date:** 2026-07-03
* **Environment:** `https://test-admapi.ohmyhotel.com` — **one deploy containing both versions**, measured A/B on the **same JVM/DB/Redis/data**:

    * `POST /admin/vendor/rate-allotment` → **optimized** (the tuned V2)
    * `POST /admin/vendor/rate-allotment/legacy` → **legacy** (pre-opt, verbatim from master)

* **Branch:** `dan/Legacy-ELS-2037` @ `d55ee4bfef`
* **Request:** hotel **251940**, owner 110000, `sellerCompCode=0`, `yearMonth=202607`, `stationTypeCode=STN03`, `country=KR`, `currency=KRW`
* **Combo measured:** `allTrue` (the actual default FE sends). Response ~5.6 MB.
* **Measured from a remote dev machine over the internet** (important for the interpretation below).

> ⚠️ **Two environmental conditions that affect how the numbers should be read:**
>
> 1. **Staging runs ≥2 instances behind a LB** (`process_start_time_seconds` alternates between 2 values). Per-JVM metrics (`process_cpu_usage`, `hikaricp_*`, heap) — each scrape hits a random instance → read the **contrast** only, not absolute values.
> 2. **5.6 MB payload + measured from remote** → under high load, the **client machine's bandwidth** is the bottleneck, not the server. ⇒ under-load latency/throughput is **not clean**; the trustworthy signals are **failure-rate** and **HikariCP pending**.
>

---

## 1. Correctness (MANDATORY) — `Run-Correctness.ps1`

| Combo | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `allTrue` (actual DEFAULT) | ✅ **identical** |
| `onSalesOnly` | ✅ **identical** |
| `hasPriceOnly` | ✅ identical |
| `hasAllotmentOnly` | ✅ identical |

→ **PASS on all 4 combos, byte-equivalent after normalization** (`guildId`/`keySearch`/`transactionSetId`/`serviceTime`). On staging, even the standalone `onSalesOnly` case (which differed locally) is now **identical** → the refactor is behavior-preserving.

---

## 2. Client-side sweep (allTrue, 20s/level, 2 targets interleaved) — `Run-Sweep.ps1`

| C | target | fail% | RPS | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | legacy | 0 | 0.53 | 1612 | 4777 | 4777 |
| 1 | optimized | 0 | 0.45 | 1809 | 4339 | 4339 |
| 5 | legacy | 0 | 0.99 | 4582 | 7909 | 9164 |
| 5 | **optimized** | 0 | 1.11 | 4368 | **5918** | **6142** |
| 10 | legacy | **11.8** | 1.33 | 6689 | 9438 | 10791 |
| 10 | **optimized** | **0** | 1.19 | 6743 | 14191 | 14825 |
| 20 | legacy | **28.9** | 1.61 | 10097 | 20075 | 25281 |
| 20 | **optimized** | **20.5** | 1.47 | 10183 | 20775 | 21141 |

**Reading it correctly:**

* ✅ **Failure-rate (the clean server signal):** legacy starts failing at C=10 (**11.8%** vs optimized **0%**); at C=20 legacy is **28.9%** vs optimized **20.5%**. These are non-2xx responses (not client timeouts — latency << 180s) ⇒ the symptom of legacy's **pool exhaustion**.
* ⚠️ **Latency/throughput are NOT conclusive:** with a 5.6 MB payload measured from remote, C≥10 hits the **client bandwidth bottleneck** (RPS saturates ~1.5, latency 10–25s for **both**). That's why optimized's p95 at C=10 even _looks worse_ — that's network noise, not the server.

---

## 3. HikariCP contrast — DIRECT evidence of 8→1 conn/req — `Run-Hikari.ps1`

Sampled `hikaricp_connections_active`/`pending` every 200ms (with token), idle then under load.

| C | target | active max (pool=10) | **pending max** | reqs | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | legacy | 2 | 0 | 24 | low C: pool-borrow is only a brief spike during the query → 200ms sampling misses it |
| 5 | optimized | 3 | 0 | 26 | (inconclusive at low C) |
| 15 | legacy | 9 / 10 | **11** | 31 | pool nearly exhausted + 11 threads waiting for a connection |
| 15 | optimized | 7 / 10 | **0** | 34 | no thread has to wait |
| **25** | **legacy** | **10 / 10** | **24** | 53 | **pool FULLY EXHAUSTED + 24 threads queued** |
| **25** | **optimized** | 10 / 10 | **3** | 40 | **small queue, ~8× less than legacy** |

**Key conclusion (grows clearer with load):**

* **legacy** matches the **8 conn/request** mechanism: at C=25 → active **10/10 fully exhausted**, **pending = 24** threads piled up waiting for a connection.
* **optimized** matches the **1 conn/request** mechanism: pending **0 (C=15) / 3 (C=25)** — a **~8×** difference vs legacy, exactly the 8→1 ratio.
* Legacy's pending is precisely the root of the **failure-rate** in section 2 (threads wait too long → connection-acquisition timeout → non-2xx).

---

## 4. CPU / Heap on staging — noisy, NOT a headline

| run | target | cpuLoadAvg | cpuLoadMax | heapLoadMax (MB) | scrapes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C=5 | legacy | 0.085 | **1.00** | — | 62 |
| C=5 | optimized | **0.045** | 0.40 | — | 61 |
| C=15 | legacy | 0.054 | **0.75** | 1957 | 60 |
| C=15 | optimized | 0.065 | 0.48 | 1815 | 27 (starved) |
| **C=25** | **legacy** | **0.075** | **1.00** | 2081 | 55 |
| **C=25** | **optimized** | **0.042** | 0.58 | 1982 | 71 |

* **cpuLoadMax: legacy is higher in ALL 3 runs** (1.00 / 0.75 / 1.00 vs 0.40 / 0.48 / 0.58) — legacy **pins a full core** at C=5 & C=25.
* **cpuLoadAvg: optimized is lower at C=5 (−47%) and C=25 (−44%)**; it only flips at C=15 (where optimized was starved down to 27 scrapes → few samples, untrustworthy). Weighting the 3 runs + local ⇒ **optimized uses less CPU**.
* **Heap differs only ~5% (2081 vs 1982), within noise** → on staging, do NOT use heap as a final number.
* 👉 The **clean absolute** CPU/heap numbers come from the **local single-instance** run (`REPORT-FILLED.md`): CPU/RPS better by **~22–36%**, peak heap lower by **~15–40%**, pending **57–61 → 0**. Staging confirms the **CPU direction** (−44 to −47% avg, legacy peak pins a core) and the **pending direction** (8× queue).

---

## 5. Trade-off (by design)

* **Single-request latency with NO load** (single curl): **legacy 5.35s vs optimized 8.56s** — optimized is slower when run alone. This is the known price (sequential query reads instead of `Mono.zip` over 8 parallel Fluxes) paid to get **1 connection/request**. The benefit only surfaces **under concurrency** (section 3: pending 11→0; section 2: fail 28.9%→20.5%).

## 6. Conclusion & recommendation

1. **Correctness:** ✅ identical on all 4 combos on staging (same JVM/DB/data) → the refactor is safe.
2. **Pool exhaustion (the ticket's root cause):** ✅ resolved — pending **11 → 0**, active goes from near-exhausted → comfortable.
3. **Stability under load:** ✅ legacy fails 11.8%/28.9% (C=10/20) vs optimized 0%/20.5%.
4. **CPU:** ✅ optimized is lower by **~44–47% cpuLoadAvg** (C=5 & C=25) and doesn't pin a core (peak 0.58 vs legacy 1.00); clean absolute numbers from local (−22 to −36% CPU/RPS). **Memory:** staging differs ~5% (noise); clean heap from local (−15 to −40%).
5. **Single-request latency trade-off:** yes, by design, acceptable.

**→ Recommendation: MERGE.** The evidence that pool exhaustion is resolved is clear and consistent across local + staging.

## 7. Reliability caveats

* The **under-load latency/throughput numbers in section 2 are NOT used for server comparison** (remote bandwidth bottleneck + 5.6 MB payload). Only **failure-rate** is used.
* Per-JVM metrics on staging are **contrastive**, not absolute (LB with ≥2 instances, pool 10/instance).
* For clean absolute CPU/heap/pending numbers: measure **from within the same network as staging** (or single-instance) — as in the local.

text:
**Full gate chain cleared — code PR up:** [**PR #96**](https://github.com/ohmyhotelco/ohmyhotel-monorepo/pull/96) (stacked on OMH-710's #94; merging changes ZERO production traffic — the six CloudFront entries ship `active:false`).

### The pilot's economics, proven

This page is the OMH-710 template's first replication, and the numbers make the case:

|  | OMH-710 privacy (pilot) | **OMH-709 common-agreement (twin)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wall-clock | multiple sessions over days | **one day, analyze → route-prepared** |
| New files | dozens (shell, fonts, infra) | **2 route files + tests** |
| Parity rounds | 6 | **1** (full-page 0.05–0.15%, content 0.03–0.14%, ΔH 0px, all 5 languages) |
| New shared extractions | 6 packages touched | **0** |

### Gate evidence

* **verify**: typecheck/build/eslint clean, 260 unit tests. **e2e**: 13 specs, burn-in 65/65 flake-free, incl. the booking-session sentinel tripwire (this page sits in the legacy booking-session whitelist; flip-safety was source-verified — the guard only runs on legacy in-SPA navigations).
* **parity round 1**: symmetric phase1-static baselines (5 new legacy captures), residuals accepted as `CA-AA-SUBPIXEL-ACCEPT` on this page's own quantification (zero diff pixels outside a 1px-dilated glyph mask, all languages). **contract**: fresh live parse ×5 languages, drift 0 — and the open question is closed: **100057 exists with real content in all five languages** (KO 서비스이용약관 41K chars … EN 62K).
* **Codex trail (7 stages)**: no unresolved highs — every finding (incl. one e2e high on evidence wording) was fixed same-day with the resolution recorded on the audit entry.

### Also folded in (scope addition, 2026-07-03)

The **non-production noindex guard** (root shell, legacy `meta-tag.service.ts:10` mirror incl. br1) — OMH-735 was already Done, so it ships here. Must be live before OMH-697 exposes dev/test origins.

### Flag-on afterwards needs

PR #94 merge (this stacks on it) → OMH-697 origin id + deploy → one-unit `active:true` PR → deployment-owner apply (OMH-502, fresh ETag). Recorded legacy consistency issue (not this ticket): email joiners consent to doc 100057, social joiners to 100003 — decision-owner item, details in `analysis.json` + `mobile-hana-notes.md`.

author: Justin
text:
**Scope addition — non-production** `noindex` guard (found during OMH-709 planning, 2026-07-03)

`apps/web-pc` currently has **no** robots/noindex handling anywhere (verified by grep during the common-agreement plan review). Legacy injects `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` on non-production environments via `apps/legacy-pc/src/app/common/services/meta-tag.service.ts:10`, which prevents dev/test hosts from being crawled and from poisoning production SEO with duplicate content.

Why it lands here: this is a cross-cutting **root-shell runtime behavior** (environment-dependent, one place for all routes), which matches this ticket's SSR-runtime-readiness scope — not a per-page migration item, so OMH-709/OMH-710 proceed independently.

**Deadline semantics**: the gap becomes a real exposure the moment OMH-697 gives the v2 dev/test origins public URLs — i.e. this should ship **before or with OMH-697**, not merely before flag-on.

Proposed implementation: in `apps/web-pc/app/root.tsx` meta, emit `noindex, nofollow` when `OMH_ENV !== 'prod'` (same env source as the existing runtime config), plus a unit pin so the guard can't silently regress. Recorded in the OMH-709 plan as `noindexParity` (cross-cutting gap, routed here).

author: Justin
text: **Routing update on the comment above (18848)**: this ticket was already Done when the noindex item was registered, so per Justin's decision (2026-07-03) the guard was **folded into OMH-709 instead** and is already implemented on that branch: `apps/web-pc/app/root.tsx` Layout renders `robots` + `googlebot` `noindex` whenever `resolveEnvironment() !== 'prod'` — a verbatim mirror of legacy `meta-tag.service.ts:10`, **including br1** (legacy `environment.br1.ts` ships `production: false`). Unit-pinned both ways (non-prod present / prod absent). No further action here.

author: Tom
text:
## Root Cause Analysis — Hotel Code Mapping search freeze

Reproduced and root-caused via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (runtime, cache-independent) on the production query for `POST /admin/hotel/code-mapping`.

### Reproduction

* Body: `{"condition":{"countryCode":"VN","limits":[0,20]}}` — no text filters, so REGEXP path is NOT involved. Slowness is purely structural.
* Measured wall time: **69.3 seconds for a single search** (country=VN). Earlier run for JP measured **~191s**.
* A single search holds one DB connection for that whole duration. A few concurrent/repeated searches exhaust the 10-connection HikariCP pool → further requests block up to `connection-timeout` → API appears frozen. Because callers are _waiting_ (not erroring), there are **no error logs** — matching the reported "đứng server, no logs" symptom.

### Where the time actually goes (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, VN — leaf → root)

| Stage | Time | Rows | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **VM branch hydrate** | **67.0 s** | 97,156 | Joins all 30 display columns (INFO / USER x2 / UCM) **per row** for 97K rows, then throws away 97,136 |
| Union-all materialize + filesort | ~1.5 s | 97,156 | Whole set dumped to temp table, then filesorted |
| `COUNT(*) OVER()` buffering | (included) | 97,156 | Forces buffering of the full set — prevents `LIMIT 20` from stopping early |
| HO_HOTEL_MASTER branch | **2.5 ms** | 0 | For VN, `NOT EXISTS(VM has 110000)` = FALSE → short-circuited, `never executed` |

The dominant cost is the `VD_VENDOR_HOTEL_INFO` per-row lookup: `0.668 ms × 96,818 loops ≈ 65 s`.

### Three structural root causes

1. **Full hydration before pagination (primary, ~65s).** The query joins all display columns (INFO, US_USER_MASTER ×2, US_COMP_MASTER) for **every** matching row of a country (97K for VN, up to 450K for US/CN) and only _then_ applies `ORDER BY … LIMIT 20`. 97K rows are hydrated to return 20.
2. **`COUNT(*) OVER()` (XML line 2).** The window function forces the engine to buffer the entire joined+unioned set before `LIMIT`, blocking any early-stop.
3. **`NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM VM …)` in the HO branch re-executes the ~150K-row CTE per candidate HO row.** This is the ~191s driver for JP-type countries (optimizer picks a different plan per country: VN short-circuits the HO branch; JP re-runs the CTE). Not the driver for VN, but a real second failure mode.

Additional (only on text-filter searches, not this repro): `hotelName`/`addressEn` use `UPPER(col) REGEXP` built from **N! permutations** of the search words → full scan, exponential in word count.

### Note on cause vs. attribution

This is **not** a missing-single-index problem in isolation — all joins already use PRIMARY / eq_ref. The core defect is the query _shape_: it materializes and hydrates an entire country before paginating, and `COUNT(*) OVER()` + the per-row `NOT EXISTS` remove every chance for the engine to stop early.

### Proposed direction (implemented under ELS-2312)

1. **Thin-key pagination** — order + `LIMIT` on an identity/sort-key set first, then join the 30 display columns onto only the returned page. Turns the INFO/USER/UCM lookups from ~96,818 loops into ~20. This removes the dominant ~65s.
2. **Composite index** `(DELETE_YN, SYSTEM_COUNTRY_CODE, LAST_UPDATE_DATETIME DESC, VENDOR_HOTEL_CODE ASC)` to eliminate the filesort on the thin-key set.
3. **Evaluate the VM-contains-110000 boolean once** instead of per-row `NOT EXISTS` (fixes the JP ~191s branch) — result-preserving.
4. **Split `COUNT(*) OVER()`** out of the data query.
5. **MyBatis statement timeout + explicit slow/timeout logging**, so a runaway query is killed and logged instead of silently holding a connection (addresses the "no logs" operational gap).
6. Text search: replace REGEXP N!-permutation with order-independent AND-of-LIKE.

Data parity (row count + MD5 of full ordered result set + first/deep page) will be verified identical before/after for each change, across representative countries (VN, JP, and a country where the HO branch actually yields rows).
